html:
A wave of peaceful protests for Korean independence from Japan that began on 1 March 1919 and spread across the country for months. Japan put it down with great violence.

Korea had been a Japanese colony since 1910. Two events sparked the protests: the death of the former emperor Gojong in January 1919, rumoured to be poisoning, and US President Wilson's call for the self-determination of nations after the First World War.

On 1 March, 33 religious leaders, from the Cheondoist, Christian and Buddhist communities, signed a Declaration of Independence in Seoul. Students read it aloud in a park, and crowds poured into the streets shouting "Long live Korean independence". Over the next months hundreds of thousands joined protests in towns across Korea.

Japanese police and troops shot into crowds, burned villages and arrested tens of thousands; thousands were killed. The schoolgirl Yu Gwan-sun died in prison and became a national symbol. The movement led to a Korean Provisional Government in Shanghai,. 1 March is a national holiday in South Korea.
sum: A wave of peaceful protests for Korean independence from Japan that began on 1 March 1919 and spread across the country for months. Japan put it down with great violence.
